description: baseline validated locally; geomean benchmark captured before launching workers

Replace torch.geqrf with a CUDA C++ batched Householder QR path specialized for the dominant n=512 batch=640 cases, using one block or cooperative tile per matrix and preserving the compact H,tau contract.
Tried cuBLAS SgeqrfBatched 512 fast path, but torch extension build failed because the locked build environment could not find ninja.
Added PATH repair for ninja and row-major/column-major staging, but build still failed because cuBLAS geqrfBatched needs per-matrix tau pointer arrays and the pybind stub needs a declaration.
Fixed the cuBLAS geqrfBatched build with tau pointer arrays, but validation rejected the extension because explicit CUDA stream usage is banned by the leaderboard guards.
Removed banned explicit stream references and built the cuBLAS geqrfBatched path, but validation hung for over seven minutes on the shape suite, making this path impractical.

Implemented a one-block-per-matrix 512x512 Householder geqr2 CUDA kernel; it built, but validation rejected 512 cases because the pybind vector return arrived as a list rather than the required tuple.

Custom one-block 256-thread 512x512 Householder geqr2 kernel validates across tests and guards, but benchmark geomean regresses versus torch.geqrf because the 512 batch shapes take about 1.04-1.07s each.
Increased the custom 512x512 geqr2 block to 512 threads. It still validated but worsened geomean to 120675.526 us, with 512 benchmark cases slower than the 256-thread version.

Returned branch head to the validated 256-thread custom geqr2 kernel and profiled it. The metric remains 118461.429 us; ncu shows low achieved occupancy and too few blocks for the 80-matrix profiled launch, explaining why this direct per-matrix kernel cannot beat torch.geqrf.

Brief 0 exhausted. I replaced torch.geqrf for n=512 with both cuBLAS geqrfBatched and custom CUDA C++ Householder paths. cuBLAS either violated stream guards or hung validation. The custom one-block 512x512 geqr2 kernel passed full validation and guards, but best geomean was 118461.429 us versus the 116405.806 us baseline; 512-thread tuning worsened to 120675.526 us. Profiling shows low achieved occupancy/too few blocks and the inherently serial column update structure, so this brief's custom per-matrix Householder direction is not promising without a deeper blocked/parallel trailing-update algorithm.

Build a true multi-CTA blocked CUDA QR prototype for n=512 rank-deficient or reduced-width batches: avoid the exhausted one-block serial-column design by using warp-reduced panel Householder kernels plus separate coalesced trailing-update kernels with many CTAs per matrix; preserve tau=0 shortcut semantics and keep torch.geqrf fallback unless this route beats current best.

Added a guarded CUDA C++ n=512 rank-deficient fast path that detects exact zero columns 384:512, factors only the first 384 columns with a custom Householder kernel, sets tail tau to zero, and falls back to torch.geqrf otherwise. It validates and improves geomean to 114593.408 us, mostly by reducing the rankdef 512 benchmark to about 679 ms.

Split zero-tail detection from the rankdef QR kernel so mixed/non-rankdef 512 cases can fall back after only a cheap detection pass. Validation passes and geomean improves to 112775.790 us; mixed 512 now returns to about 969 ms while rankdef remains about 677 ms.

Added a batch>=256 gate to avoid zero-tail detection on small n=512 test-like calls. It validates but slightly regresses geomean to 112853.888 us, so this gate is not better than the split-dispatch version.
Restored the best split zero-tail detection dispatch as branch head after the batch gate regressed. Effective metric remains the best measured 112775.790 us.
Tried reducing the exact-zero-tail QR cutoff to 256 columns. It validates but rankdef 512 jumps back to about 959 ms and geomean regresses to 116262.119 us, so rank=384 is the useful cutoff.
Restored the best rank=384 split-dispatch implementation after rank=256 regressed. Branch head is back to the best measured geomean 112775.790 us.

Brief 1 exhausted. A true broad multi-CTA panel/update implementation was not reached in a maintainable form, but the on-brief reduced-width idea produced a valid CUDA C++ n=512 exact-zero-tail fast path. Best result is commit 4a4549da / implementation equivalent to 7978e77b: split zero-tail detection plus rank=384 Householder QR for rankdef matrices, falling back to torch.geqrf otherwise. It improves geomean from baseline 116405.806 us to 112775.790 us. Rank=256 and batch gating were tried and regressed; profile still shows low occupancy for the one-block QR kernel, suggesting the next brief should either stack this improvement with other shape-specific paths or invest in a genuinely multi-CTA trailing-update kernel for the rank=384 tail case.

Micro-tune the 7978e77 n=512 rankdef CUDA path only: profile detector, all-flags synchronization, allocation, and geqr2_rankdef_512 time; test one local change per commit, prioritizing eliminating torch.all sync or unnecessary h/tau writes, and keep only variants beating 112775.790 while preserving dense and mixed fallback behavior.

Replaced per-matrix flags plus torch.all with a one-element atomic bad-count detector to reduce Python all-flags overhead. It validates, but geomean regresses to 112888.220 us, likely due to atomic/zero allocation overhead and slightly slower rankdef path.
Restored the parent flags detector after scalar bad-count regressed. Branch head is back to the 112775.790 us implementation.

Changed geqr2_rankdef_512 to copy only the first 384 columns and explicitly zero the known zero tail in H. It validates and slightly improves the rankdef shape, but other shapes/noise make geomean regress to 112863.948 us, so the full copy parent remains best.
Restored the parent full-copy rankdef implementation after copy elision regressed the aggregate. Branch head is again the 112775.790 us parent.

Brief 2 exhausted. I micro-tuned only the 7978e77 rankdef CUDA path. Replacing flags+torch.all with a scalar atomic bad-count detector validated but regressed to 112888.220 us. Copying only the first 384 H columns and zeroing the tail validated and slightly improved the rankdef shape, but aggregate regressed to 112863.948 us. Both were reverted; branch head is b2bd33ca, equivalent to the parent 7978e77, with metric 112775.790 us. Final profile still shows low achieved occupancy and only 80 blocks in the captured kernel, so no local micro tweak beat the parent.

Attack the n=512 mixed benchmark with fraction-aware per-matrix CUDA C++ dispatch: use the existing zero-tail detector to count and flag rankdef matrices, compact indices and run custom rank=384 QR only when the rankdef count exceeds a threshold, send dense matrices to torch.geqrf, scatter outputs back in original order, and benchmark thresholds against current all-or-nothing fallback.

Added a thresholded mixed n=512 dispatcher using zero-tail flags: when at least 64 matrices are rankdef, compact rankdef indices to custom rank=384 QR, run torch.geqrf on dense indices, then scatter outputs. It validates, but geomean regresses to 112920.134 us; mixed 512 remains around 969 ms and extra compaction/scatter overhead outweighs benefits.

Lowered mixed split threshold to 1 so any rankdef matrix triggers compaction/custom QR for flagged matrices and torch.geqrf for dense matrices. It validates but mixed 512 worsens to about 1.028 s and geomean regresses to 113563.479 us.

Restored the all-or-nothing split zero-tail parent after mixed per-matrix dispatch variants regressed. Branch head is back to parent semantics with target metric 112668.376/112775.790 depending run noise.

Brief 3 exhausted. I implemented fraction-aware per-matrix mixed dispatch on top of the split zero-tail detector: compact rankdef indices to custom rank=384 QR, route dense indices through torch.geqrf, and scatter outputs. Threshold 64 validated but regressed to 112920.134 us; threshold 1 validated but regressed further to 113563.479 us because mixed 512 slowed to about 1.028 s. Both variants were worse than all-or-nothing fallback, so branch head f9ade3c9 restores parent semantics from 22ac8539. Final profile saved; recommendation is not to pursue Python-level compaction/scatter for mixed batches unless compaction and dense/custom QR can be fused in CUDA without torch index_select/index_copy overhead.

Replace the rank=384 one-block geqr2 path for n=512 exact rankdef with a multi-CTA CUDA C++ QR trailing-update design: keep detector and fallback unchanged, allow panel generation to start single-CTA, but distribute Householder trailing updates across column-tile CTAs with coalesced loads and shared or broadcast reflector data; explore tile shapes from profiles and keep only if n=512 rankdef improves and total geomean beats 112668.376 with correctness preserved.

Added a multi-launch rankdef QR prototype with separate init, per-column panel, and column-tile update kernels, but validation hit cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration when the update grid had zero columns at the final panel.

Fixed the zero-column update-grid bug in the multi-CTA rankdef QR prototype. It validates and distributes trailing updates across (batch,column) CTAs, but thousands of panel/update launches make rankdef 512 slower (~799 ms) and geomean regresses to 114496.908 us.
Restored the split zero-tail parent after the launch-synchronized multi-CTA QR design regressed. Branch head is back to parent semantics, target metric 112668.376.

Brief 4 exhausted. I built a launch-synchronized multi-CTA rank=384 QR prototype: init kernel, per-panel single-CTA Householder generation, and per-column trailing-update CTAs across (batch,column). First attempt hit cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration at the final zero-width update grid and was logged as validation_error. Fixing that made the design validate, but benchmark regressed to 114496.908 us because 384 panel launches plus 383 update launches dominate; n=512 rankdef worsened to about 799 ms versus ~677 ms parent. Restored parent split zero-tail implementation at head a8f7d7a3. Future multi-CTA work needs a persistent/cooperative kernel or grouped-panel strategy to avoid per-column launch overhead.

For parent 59e2704, explore an n=512 banded-shape specialization: profile the active banded benchmark, add a conservative CUDA C++ detector for the deterministic narrow-band pattern, then specialize the existing Householder path by bounding column scans and trailing updates to the nonzero band with guarded fallback to the clustered/rankdef best; preserve FP32 QR validation and keep only if geomean beats 103221.174.

Added a conservative CUDA C++ n=512 band detector for exact bandwidth-16 matrices and an all-batch banded Householder path that bounds reflector scans and trailing updates. It validates, including the band test, and benchmark measured 103121.428 us versus parent 103221.174; active mixed still falls back because only some matrices are banded, so the small gain is likely detector/profile noise rather than a robust active-set improvement.

Extended the band detector to active n=512 mixed batches: compact detected bandwidth-16 matrices, run the custom bounded band QR on them, route the rest through torch.geqrf, then scatter H/tau back. Validation and guards pass; benchmark improves mixed 512 from ~970 ms to ~907 ms and geomean to 102840.243 us, beating parent 103221.174 despite small rankdef/clustered noise regressions.

Raised the mixed n=512 band split threshold from 32 to 64 to avoid compaction overhead on sparse-band batches. It validates, but the active mixed benchmark no longer routes to the band path and geomean regresses to 103512.326 us, worse than both parent and threshold-32; this threshold is not kept.
Reverted the threshold-64 experiment and restored the validated threshold-32 mixed band dispatcher, the best banded-shape result from this brief at 102840.243 us.

Brief 5 exhausted. Best result is the threshold-32 mixed band dispatcher restored at head 78df96c9, with measured geomean 102840.243 us versus parent 103221.174. The work added a conservative exact bandwidth-16 CUDA detector, a bounded one-block Householder QR for n=512 band matrices, and mixed-batch compaction/scatter so active mixed batches route detected band matrices to the custom path while preserving clustered/rankdef fallbacks. Homogeneous/all-band validated and threshold 64 validated but regressed to 103512.326 because it missed the active mixed band count, so threshold 32 is kept. Final validation passed and final profile saved.

Micro-tune only the n=512 mixed band dispatcher from 9b003b2: isolate detector, compaction, and scatter overhead before bounded band QR; try one local change per commit, prioritizing narrower clustered sampling, eliminating redundant index copies, and band-count thresholds 24 or 40 before QR thread/block tweaks; preserve clustered and rankdef correctness and keep only validated variants beating 102748.878.

Lowered the n=512 mixed band dispatcher threshold from 32 to 24, preserving the sampled clustered detector and all rankdef/clustered/band QR kernels. Validation and guards passed; benchmark measured 102502.486 us vs parent 102748.878, with active mixed 512 around 906.0 ms and favorable noise on rankdef/nearrank.

Raised the n=512 mixed band dispatcher threshold from 24 to 40 as an isolated threshold test. Validation and guards passed; benchmark measured 102602.767 us, still better than parent 102748.878 but worse than threshold 24 at 102502.486, so threshold 40 is not kept.
Reverted the threshold-40 experiment and restored the threshold-24 mixed band dispatcher, the best validated threshold from this brief so far at 102502.486 us.
